<problem>
For an integer $h\ge2$, a set $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ is a $B_h$ set if every $n\in\mathbb N$ has at most one representation $n=a_1+\dots+a_h$ with $a_1\le\dots\le a_h$, $a_i\in A$ (so $B_2$ sets are Sidon sets). $A$ is an asymptotic basis of order $k$ if $kA=\{a_1+\dots+a_k: a_i\in A\}$ contains every sufficiently large integer. Let $g(h)$ be the least $k$ for which some $B_h$ set is an asymptotic basis of order $k$. Since a $B_h$ set has $|A\cap[N]|\le (1+o(1))\,(h\cdot h!\,N)^{1/h}$, one has $|hA\cap[N]|\le \binom{|A\cap[N]|+h-1}{h}<N$ for large $N$, so $g(h)\ge h+1$; Pilatte's theorem gives $g(2)=3$. Question 1: Is $g(h)=h+1$ for every $h\ge3$, i.e. is there a $B_3$ set $A$ with $4A\supseteq\{n: n\ge n_0\}$? Question 2: If not, is $g(h)\le 2h$ for all $h$, or does $g(h)-h\to\infty$?
</problem>

<solution>
I did not solve either question. What I can prove: for a B_h set A with |A∩[N]| ≤ (1+o(1))(h·h!·N)^{1/h}, we get |hA∩[N]| ≤ C(|A∩[N]|+h-1, h) < N for large N, so hA cannot contain all large integers and g(h) ≥ h+1. Pilatte's theorem gives g(2)=3. Open: Question 1 (whether a B_3 set can be an asymptotic basis of order 4, and whether g(h)=h+1 for all h≥3) and Question 2 (whether g(h) ≤ 2h for all h, or g(h)-h→∞). Difficulty: a B_h basis of order h+1 has only about N^{(h+1)/h} sums of h+1 elements up to N, only a factor N^{1/h} more than needed, so the representation function must be almost perfectly regular. Pilatte's method for h=2 is a delicate probabilistic perturbation construction, and for h≥3 it is not clear how to remove the many B_h coincidences while keeping coverage. I have no proof or disproof of either statement.
</solution>
